page: Microsoft Azure E16ds_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine built on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. The instance features dedicated hardware execution via an Intel Xeon 6973P-C processor clocked at 4.2 GHz. Its x86_64 architecture provides 16 virtual CPUs derived from 8 physical cores with multithreading, backed by a large 480 MB L3 cache. The CPU configuration includes modern instruction set extensions such as AVX-512, Intel AMX for matrix multiplication, and accelerated cryptographic primitives like VAES and SHA-NI.

Resource allocation includes 128 GB of system memory, establishing an 8 GB per vCPU ratio suitable for memory-bound computing. The instance bundles 944 GB of direct-attached NVMe SSD local storage for low-latency scratch space and temporary file operations, alongside support for Azure Premium Storage. Hardware accelerators are absent, with zero GPUs provisioned on this configuration.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong data manipulation performance, driven by the updated Intel core architecture. Single-threaded gzip compression reached 36.52 GB/sec and bzip3 decompression delivered 15.37 GB/sec, placing the server in the top tier for compression tasks. Memory bandwidth recorded 136.15 GB/sec for large-block reads and 56.03 GB/sec for writes. In CPU-driven inference, text generation on a 135M parameter language model reached top-tier execution at 343.48 tokens/sec, while broader multi-core compute metrics on PassMark and stress-ng landed squarely in the median percentile.

Balancing a high memory-to-core ratio with rapid bundled NVMe storage delivers strong resource density without requiring separate ephemeral disk provisioning. The instance is well matched for in-memory databases like Redis, relational database systems, ETL data processing, and enterprise workloads requiring substantial memory buffers and fast compression throughput.
